answer: Sequential work audit: each identity must periodically submit a solution to a fresh challenge derived from the prior solution, forming an unbroken hash-linked chain (like a crystal lattice) that cannot be precomputed or copied. Verification costs one hash check, but forging N identities costs N distinct compute chains. The registry posts a new public knoll of challenge seeds every epoch, so stalled chains expire. Attacker cost is sustained parallel compute plus latency, not a one-time deposit; abandoned chains become a cold ember of wasted cycles.
